title: On-prem Geo-Boundary Enforcer and Regional Failback Constraints for Private/VPC Deployments
creator: Priya Malhotra
description:
Purpose: Implement a lightweight enforcement layer and operator-facing constraints that guarantee data storage and execution remain within declared geographic boundaries for Private/VPC/on-prem customers, while providing safe, auditable regional failback behavior when an allowed zone becomes unavailable. This ticket covers the enforcement policy, metrics to prove compliance, and an automated evidence export for audits. Scope includes control-plane enforcement hooks, node-level affinity checks, request routing policies, retention-scope markers, and the evidence/reporting automation pipeline. Out of scope: public-hosted API changes and non-Private tenants.

Non-goals: building a full legal interpretation engine or replacing customer-side contractual controls. We aim to produce technical safeguards and an auditable trail that demonstrate enforcement decisions and failback rationale.
acceptance_criteria: A1: New geo-boundary policy config exists in Private control plane with fields: allowed_zones (list), allowed_regions (list), failback_mode (deny | restricted | buffered), max-buffer-duration (ISO8601), and evidence_retention_days.
A2: Node-agent rejects scheduling or KV-cache restoration attempts for nodes outside allowed_zones unless failback_mode allows and customer explicit opt-in is recorded.

A3: Automated evidence bundle produced within 1 hour of any policy-triggering failover event containing: pre/post decision traces, routing decisions, affected request IDs, and storage shard locations; bundle cryptographically signed and stored in customer audit bucket.

A4: E2E tests simulate region outage and verify failback constraints: when failback_mode=deny, no traffic leaves allowed_zones; when restricted, traffic may use paired-regions only after multi-signed operator approval; when buffered, short bursts allowed with KV-prefix eviction and evidence capture.
A5: Console UI shows per-deployment compliance status, last evidence export timestamp, and a downloadable signed archive for auditors.
A6: Telemetry: 99% of compliance-related decisions include decision_cause tag and a trace id; exportable to compliance dashboard within 5 minutes.
A7: Security review completed and signed-off by Security & Compliance team with remediation items tracked.
A8: Documentation and runbook published and linked from the deployment details page.
success_metrics: No unauthorized cross-zone execution or storage observed in synthetic compliance tests (target 0 incidents)
Evidence bundle generation latency < 60 minutes in 95th percentile
Console compliance status accuracy > 99% against ground-truth test harness
Operator approval flow average time < 10 minutes for restricted failback scenarios (target)
design_notes:
Core idea: implement a two-layer model: (1) declarative policy at the Private control plane that defines permitted data and execution locality; (2) enforcement adapters at node-agent, router, and storage-proxy that evaluate a lightweight capability token and a signed policy-version header. Policy changes are versioned; every policy evaluation emits a signed decision event and attaches a decision_id to requests so evidence bundles can be assembled offline.

Trade-offs: Strong deny (failfast) minimizes leak risk but increases customer outage risk; buffered mode reduces downtime at the cost of temporary expanded footprint and increased evidence volume. We propose defaulting to 'restricted' for new customers but requiring explicit opt-in for 'buffered'.

Key components: policy schema, control-plane UI, node-agent enforcement, egress/routing guard, storage-proxy location validation, evidence bundler, and an auditor CLI to verify signed bundles.

Compatibility notes: must integrate with existing VPC peering and on-prem agents. Keep runtime changes minimal; most logic lives in agents and control-plane policy service.

Open questions: 1) exact retry/backoff semantics for buffered bursts, 2) crypto key rotation for bundle signing (KMS integration scope), 3) whether to support multi-tenant regional exceptions for customer-provided partner endpoints.
implementation_plan: Step 1: Define policy schema and API contract in control plane (config + policy-version endpoint)
Step 2: Extend node-agent to validate policy on startup and reject non-compliant node registration
Step 3: Router: add failover-policy evaluator that emits decision events and enforces routing constraints
Step 4: Storage-proxy: implement location check on blob writes/reads and tag objects with storage-zone metadata
Step 5: Evidence bundler service: aggregate decision events, traces, and storage metadata; produce signed archives
Step 6: Console: surface compliance status and evidence download link; add controls for operator approval flow
Step 7: Tests: add deterministic simulation harness and chaos tests (zone blackhole, delayed agent heartbeats)
Step 8: Security review and compliance sign-off, publish runbook and customer-facing documentation
rollout_plan: Phase A: Internal dogfood on sandbox Private cluster with test policies (2 weeks)
Phase B: Beta with select customers under NDA, default failback_mode=restricted (3 weeks)
Phase C: GA for Private/VPC with console controls and auto-evidence export (2 weeks)
Rollback: policy-version rollback supported; node-agent will reject newer incompatible policies until upgraded
monitoring_and_reporting: Telemetry emitted per decision: decision_id, policy_version, reason_code, affected_request_ids (sampled), node_id, region, timestamp. Compliance dashboard will show policy drift, last evidence export, and open approval requests. Evidence bundles are stored in customer audit buckets (S3/GCS) and indexed in the control plane for fast retrieval. Alerts: policy-violation (high), evidence-fail (medium), stale-agent-heartbeat (medium).
